description:

lines.text: It is four fifty five on a Friday. My boss just sent me a message.
Do you have a minute?
Oh no. Oh, Terrence. No.
It is five words, Bea. Five normal words.
Nothing good has ever started with do you have a minute.
I am just the phone. I deliver the words. I do not choose the words.
Okay. Let's read it slowly. Do you have a minute.
Read it like she wrote it. Do you have a minute.
Do. You have a minute. Like she is double checking.
Like she already asked once and you ignored her.
I did not ignore her. I was at lunch for an hour and forty minutes.
He had the soup. Twice.
Now try it this way. Do you have a minute.
Do you. Me. Not you, not Gary. Me, specifically.
Why would she skip Gary? Gary microwaves fish on purpose.
Gary is family to this office. I am a man with a stapler.
It is not even his stapler. It says Linda on the bottom.
It came with the desk!
Okay, calm down. There is one more way to read it.
Do you have a minute.
Have. Like, do you own any minutes. Like she has been counting yours.
She knows about the lunch.
She knows about the soup.
And then there is the scariest one. Do you have a minute.
A minute. Just one. My last one.
Sixty seconds to put your plant in a box and say goodbye to the printer.
The printer never liked me anyway.
Also, the little dots just showed up. She is typing.
Everybody be quiet. The dots are thinking.
The dots went away.
Why would the dots go away? What did the dots decide?
She wrote a paragraph and deleted it. That is a paragraph about you.
Okay. I have to answer her. What do I say?
Keep it short. Keep it brave. Say sure.
Sure.
Sent. With a period.
You put a period on it? A period is a door closing, Terrence.
It is a dot! It is the smallest thing on the keyboard!
It is the loudest dot I have ever sent. And I sent a lot of dots.
Now she thinks you are quitting. Or you are angry. Or you are a pirate.
Why a pirate?
I do not know, I panic in pirates.
Incoming. She is walking over here. She has her face on.
Terrence. Hi. Do you have a minute?
I said sure. With the smallest dot.
I know. I saw the dot. Are you quitting? Please tell me you are not quitting.
Me? I thought you were letting me go.
Letting you go? Terrence, there are forty people hiding in conference room B.
Why are there forty people in conference room B?
It is your five year anniversary. We have a cake. It has your face on it.
Everyone has been crouching under the table for twenty five minutes.
Gary texted. His knees are gone. He says hurry.
You wanted a minute to walk me to my own party?
I typed that message eleven times. I deleted a paragraph. It had a joke in it.
So the dots were nervous too.
The dots were terrified. Then you sent sure with a period and I sat in my car.
Linda. You are my boss. You overthink too?
Terrence, I am a boss. I overthink professionally.
Also, the stapler. She would like it back. It says Linda on the bottom.
Keep the stapler. Happy five years.
Thank you. Really. Before we go in, can I ask you something?
Of course.
Do you have a minute?
Why. What does that mean. Bea, what does that mean?
